New HRSA Audit

Upload Data Request List (DRL) Document

Attach the DRL document provided by your auditor. It'll be stored with this audit for your records and included in the supporting documents.

Drag and drop or browse a file

Only less than 10MB CSV and XLS files are supported.

description
Our-Requested-DRL from HRSA.pdf
4 MB File added — click start to upload.

Once your audit is created, you'll be able to work through each HRSA request with your team, link data from your existing workflows as supporting evidence, track progress, and generate your response package when you're ready to submit.

info After your On-Site Audit
  • Expect roughly 2 months to receive your final audit report (This is an approximate, the length of time varies audit-to-audit).
  • Maintain records of all information provided prior to or during the on-site (Audit reports may refer to a sample, but include little additional detail).
  • If you expect a finding that you will not contest, get a jump start on your Corrective Action Plan.
  • If there is a finding, you will receive 30 days to complete a Notice of Disagreement or 60 days to complete a Corrective Action Plan.

Audit Preparation Logistics

On-Site Tip

Prepare to be able to provide copies of paid Medicaid claims. This will apply to outpatient administered drugs and should demonstrate compliance with state reporting and coding requirements (UD modifiers).

Audit Name Walgreens HRSA - 2026 Q1
Request Description

All preparation needed for your on-site audit. This includes identifying key staff that will take part in the audit process, coordinating with other departments for documentation, and ensuring that there is a designated space for the auditor during their visit.

Request Lead
AN
Annabelle Narsh
Task Details
link
Linked to a HRSA Audit
keyboard_arrow_up
Title Must do X, Y, and Z
Status Active
Assignee
JS
John Snow
Due Date May 09, 2025
On-Site Preparation Items keyboard_arrow_up
1 Designate Staff

Designate staff to be with the auditor throughout the day and have an action plan for who will be speaking with the auditor. Have on-call staff available as well.

2 Contact Necessary Departments

Reach out to all necessary departments who will be involved in the audit process. You will likely want to reach out to:

  • Contract and Retail Pharmacies
  • Third Party Administrator
  • Service Provider
  • Credentialing
  • Billing
3 Create a Space
  • Reserve a room that can accommodate all attendees.
  • Ensure that all necessary systems needed for lookups are accessible from the room prior to the visit.
  • Consider projecting lookups on a screen for a smooth viewing process.
4 Maintain Records

Maintain records of all information provided prior to or during the on-site audit. Audit reports may refer to a sample, but include little additional detail.

On-Site Tip

During the on-site, the auditor will compare your Policies and Procedures with your processes. Make sure your Policies and Procedures are operationalized.

Audit Name Walgreens HRSA - 2026 Q1
Request Context See HRSA detailed info ›
  • If a hospital contracted with the state or local government: Per Section 340B Public Health Service Act, a private non-profit hospital must have a contract with a State or local government to provide health care services to low income individuals.
  • If a hospital granted governmental powers: You will be required to provide documentation that clearly illustrates that the hospital is a public corporation or a private non-profit corporation as well as proof of governmental powers.

The following are the elements that should be included within the 340B Universe.

A The drug/product name
*Required
B NDC
C The acquisition price
D Type of account, purchase account, and 340B ID Number
E The quantity issued
*Required
F The patient ID number
G The payer (all payers including Medicaid)
*Required
H Date of the drug order or prescription
I The ordering provider
*Required
J Location 340B drug was administered or prescribed
K Date the drug was administered or dispensed

infoAfter your On-Site Audit
  • Expect roughly 2 months to receive your final audit report (This is an approximate, the length of time varies audit-to-audit).

  • If you expect a finding that you will not contest, get a jump start on your Corrective Action Plan.
  • If there is a finding, you will receive 30 days to complete a Notice of Disagreement or 60 days to complete a Corrective Action Plan.

  • An audit lead and team members

340BCheck Info

Eligibility Documentation (Trial Balance)

If any offsite outpatient facilities utilize 340B drugs (at the facility or through a contract pharmacy), provide the trial balance that was submitted to CMS with the MCR(s).

The trial balance must include:

  • The 340B ID
  • Name of each offsite outpatient facility as identified in OPAIS
  • Address of all offsite outpatient facilities
  • Worksheets A & C (Line Number and Cost Center Description)
  • Trial balance name and department code/account
  • The location code or shorthand used to identify the site in the electronic health record (EHR)
  • Yes/No indication for 340B drug utilization during encounters at the site

340BCheck Info

Eligibility Documentation (Entity Status Documentation)

If a hospital contracted with the state or local government:

Per Section 340B Public Health Service Act, a private non-profit hospital must have a contract with a State or local government to provide health care services to low income individuals who are not entitled to benefits under title XVIII of the Social Security Act or eligible for assistance under the State plan under this title.

340B Check has gathered all Indigent Care Agreement (ICA) workscreens and shown all documents labeled as Final or Archived below. Verify records are up to date and copy over any required documents. Please highlight the following in the document prior to uploading through the NIH portal:

  1. The provision that the hospital must provide health care services to low income individuals who are not entitled to benefits under Title XVIII of the Social Security Act or eligible for assistance under the State plan under this title;
  2. Names of the hospital and the government agency;
  3. Signatures of hospital and government agency representatives; and
  4. Effective dates of the contract.
info

A copy of the contract / documentation that demonstrates the hospital’s private nonprofit status must also be provided. Proof of status may be the following: the hospital’s charter, articles of incorporation, bylaws, other State documents that certify the hospital is non-profit, a copy of the latest filed IRS 990 form, or other official IRS documentation.

If a hospital granted governmental powers:

You will be required to provide documentation that clearly illustrates that the hospital is a public corporation or a private non-profit corporation as well as proof of governmental powers.

info

Examples of proof of public corporation status include: copy of the law that created the hospital, documentation from the government that illustrates ownership, the hospital’s charter, bylaws, or IRS documentation.

340BCheck Info

Eligibility Documentation (Entity Status Documentation)

info

More than one document may be necessary to demonstrate eligibility. Any documentation should clearly state the hospital’s ownership, the date the ownership was established, and the name of the hospital.

Hospital entities keyboard_arrow_down

If the hospital is owned or operated by a state or local government:

  • Provide documentation that indicates that the hospital is owned or operated by a state or local government
  • This may include the law that created the hospital, the hospital’s charter, the hospital’s bylaws, documentation from the IRS describing the hospital, or documentation from the state or local government that clearly demonstrates ownership

If the hospital is a private nonprofit with a contract with a unit of state or local government to provide health care services to low-income individuals:

  • Provide a copy of the contract and documentation that demonstrates the hospital’s private nonprofit status
  • Highlight the provision that the hospital must provide health care services to low-income individuals who are not entitled to benefits under Title XVII of the Social Security Act or eligible for assistance under the state plan under this title, the names of the hospital and the government agency, the signatures of the hospital and government representatives, and the effective date of the contract
  • This may include the hospital’s charter, the hospital’s bylaws, the hospital’s articles of incorporation, a copy of the hospital’s latest filed IRS Form 990, other official IRS documentation, or other documentation from the state that may certify that the hospital is nonprofit

If the hospital is a public corporation or private nonprofit corporation that is formally granted governmental powers by a unit of state or local government:

  • Provide documentation that demonstrates the hospital’s status
    • For public corporation hospitals, this may include a copy of the law that created the hospital, the hospital’s charter, the hospital’s bylaws, documentation from the IRS describing the hospital, or documentation from the state or local government that clearly demonstrates ownership
    • For private nonprofit hospitals, this may include the hospital’s charter, the hospital’s bylaws, the hospital’s articles of incorporation, a copy of the hospital’s latest filed IRS Form 990, other official IRS documentation, a copy of the 501(c)(3) certification, or other documentation from the state that may certify that the hospital is a nonprofit
  • Provide documentation that confers governmental powers, which should contain ALL of the following elements:
    • Identity of the government entity granting the governmental powers
    • Description of the governmental power that has been granted to the hospital and a brief explanation as to why the power is considered to be governmental
    • Official documentation issued by the government to the hospital granting formal governmental powers
Grantee entities keyboard_arrow_down

For all grantee entities:

  • Provide a copy of the notice of grant award or designation of look-alike status (for all grantees except FQHC638 entities), or a copy of the tribal contract/compact with Indian Health Service (for FQHC638 entities only)
  • Sub-grantee documentation may include the Notice of Funding Award between the primary grantee and sub-grantee, the Notice of Grant Award project narrative that clearly indicates the sub-grantee’s receipt of funding, or the in-kind support (e.g., contracts, agreements, or memoranda of understanding).
info

Documents should list the grantor, grant number, period of funding, the primary grantee by name and address, and the sub-grantee service location(s) by name and address. In addition, if the grant is listed in HRSA’s Electronic Handbooks (EHBs), include Form 5A (scope of services) and Form 5B (service locations).

340BCheck Info

340B Universe

What to include in the report?

Provide a listing of all 340B drugs that were furnished, administered, or prescribed to patients from the parent site, offsite facilities/grant-associated sites, and pharmacies (in-house/entity-owned and contracted) during the sample period.

Include a narrative describing the methodology, and system/software from which the data was gathered, and any limitations or exclusions (e.g. whether reversed transactions, or any other elements, were excluded or other 340B orders or dispenses, were direct purchases included or other purchasing mechanisms). Define each area(s) of service on the spreadsheet(s) with column heading’s name and indicate which area the spreadsheet represents.

info

This report should be scrubbed to remove any non-340B drugs (e.g. vaccines, syringes, products defined as non-covered outpatient drugs) including orphans (for SCH, CAH, CAN, and RRC entities) when applicable, definition for Split Billing (drug orders), and separate for Contract Pharmacy (prescriptions).

On-site information:

A sample of prescriptions will be selected for testing while the audit team is on site/during the on-site/remote site visit audit. For the selected items, individual records will need to be available in either electronic or paper format.

If electronic health records (ERHs) are utilized, be sure to provide an individual with system knowledge to navigate the EHR (including billing information) and the split-billing software/third-party.

info

Ensure that no protected health information (PHI) or personally identifiable information (PII) such as a patient’s name, date of birth, or address is submitted in the data request list uploads.

340BCheck Info

340B Universe. Elements required for report:

A. The drug/product name *required

keyboard_arrow_up
The drug name will be the charge code description. Include CDM. Best practice is to not include NDC unless it’s the only identifier available.

B. NDC

C. The acquisition price

keyboard_arrow_down
Don’t include unless complete and accurate for all records. Can be found in the purchasing history. Ensure 340B universe includes a statement in regard to this. Purchasing history can be used to identify acquisition cost.

D. The type of account the drug was purchased through, purchase account, and the associated 340B ID number

keyboard_arrow_down
Don’t include unless complete and accurate for all records. Can be found in the purchasing history. Ensure 340B universe includes a statement in regard to this. Purchasing history can be used to identify acquisition cost.

E. The quantity issued *required

keyboard_arrow_down
First choice is CDM qty. Include only one column related to quantity. Remove any package sizes.

F. The patient ID number

keyboard_arrow_down
This is typically the medical record number or prescription number, but can be any number you assigned that will allow tracking through the entity’s system to retrieve all information associated with the order.

G. The payer (all payers including Medicaid) *required for split billing

keyboard_arrow_down
Some TPAs for contract/retail will not include this (Walgreens includes payer categories. i.e. third party, Medicare, commercial, etc). Prescriptions will have BIN/PCNs/Group ID, this is acceptable. Only include the primary. If secondary and tertiary are provided, review but do not submit to HRSA.

H. Date the drug order or prescription was written (for hospital-administered drugs, also include the time the drug was ordered)

keyboard_arrow_down

Time stamps – only include in HRSA submission if accurate and complete. Keep time stamps in the file. Be sure to remove time altogether from HRSA submission, not just convert to short date.

  • Prescriptions: include date prescribed/written and date of service/fill. The date of service/fill should be used to pull the report for the audit timeframe. DON’T USE PROCESSED DATES!
  • Split Billing: date of service; this should be the date the patient received the medication. *WellPartner states date of dispense. This should be changed to date of service.

I. The ordering provider *required

keyboard_arrow_down
Name only for HRSA submission. NPI/DEA required for review. This is optional for Split Billing. If included and there are significant gaps or inaccuracies, delete. If minimal gaps, review with client.

J. Location/Site 340B drug was furnished/administered/ordered (mixed-use pharmacy) or prescribed (in-house or contract pharmacy)

keyboard_arrow_down
Optional = Prescription – Pharmacy dispensing name. If the 340B ID is accurately provided, include. For split billing this will be the location code/mnemonic/name in the EMR. Please also provide a cross-walk for the location codes to the full location name, addresses and 340B IDs.

K. Date the drug was furnished, administered, or dispensed

keyboard_arrow_down
Available for prescriptions only. This will not be included in the split-billing software. Ignore for report, address in the 340B Universe.
340BCheck Info

Drug Purchasing Documentation

The covered entity will need to provide:

  1. A listing of all accounts (wholesaler, direct and consignment) used to purchase or ship drugs for the parent, off-site facilities, all pharmacies (in-house/entity-owned and contracted), or any other locations (e.g., repackagers, distribution center, etc.). Include the following for each account:

a. Wholesaler name

b. Account number

c. Account name

d. Pricing associated with the account (340B, GPO, WAC, etc.)

e. For 340B accounts, the 340B ID associated with the account (i.e., the 340B ID used to open/establish the account

f. Name and address of the location that receives the drugs from the wholesaler or manufacturer, including 340B ID if applicable

g. A description of the location that receives the drugs (e.g., mixed-use pharmacy, entity-owned pharmacy, infusion pharmacy, contract pharmacy, health care service delivery site for clinic/physician-administered drugs, repackager, distribution center, etc.)

h. An answer to the following question: "Is the account used in a controlled substance ordering system (CSOS)?" (yes or no)

i. An answer to the following question: "Does the location that receives the drugs furnish, administer, or dispense those drugs directly to patients in person or by mail?" (yes or no)

j. An answer to the following question: "If the location that initially receives drugs from the wholesaler or manufacturer redistributes those drugs to other location(s), what is the name, address, and 340B ID, if applicable, of the location(s) the drugs are redistributed to?"

  1. Provide a copy of one invoice for each account identified in the listing of accounts requested above.
  1. Listing of covered entity's (parent, off-site facilities, and contract pharmacies) 340B drug purchase orders made within the audit sample period. Include the following data elements in the listing:

a. Ordering location (parent, off-site facility, or contract pharmacy)

b. Wholesaler name

c. Account number

d. Invoice number

e. Invoice date

f. Drug description

g. Drug NDC

h. Quantity ordered

i. Price paid

info

Excel format is preferred for account and purchase order listings.

340BCheck Info

Contract Pharmacy Documentation

The covered entity should be prepared to provide a listing of all contract pharmacies during the audit sample period. For each contract pharmacy, identify whether the pharmacy is utilized or not utilized by the covered entity. Provide all contract pharmacy agreements and any related amendments.

info

PDF format is preferred for all documents.

The covered entity will need to provide:

  1. A list of all of the covered entity’s contract pharmacies from the beginning of the audit sample period through the date of the on-site/remote audit. For each contract pharmacy location, indicate whether the pharmacy is used by the covered entity.
  1. For each contract pharmacy, provide the original agreement and any amendments or addenda. Highlight the following areas in each contract pharmacy agreement/amendment/addendum:
  • Signatures of all parties executing the contract, including dates
  • Name and address for each contract pharmacy location participating in the contract pharmacy agreement
  • Each covered entity location by name and address or general statement that inclusively identifies the parent and all covered entity location(s) participating in the contract pharmacy agreement
info

Include those pharmacies that may have been terminated since the start of the audit timeframe.

  1. Provide a cover page or statement on letterhead from the organization that conducted the last independent audit of the covered entity’s contract pharmacies. The document should include:
  • Audit date
  • Period audited
  • Who performed the audit
  • Scope of the audit
  1. Provide supporting documentation of any internal contract pharmacy audits conducted by the covered entity from the start of the sample period through the date of the audit.
  1. Provide a list of all Medicaid fee-for-service BIN and PCN numbers that are carved out at contract pharmacy contract locations (i.e., provides non-340B drugs to patients with Medicaid fee-for-service).
g
Not Covered

340BCheck Info

Medicaid Billing Documentation

Provide Medicaid fee-for-service billing documentation for each covered entity site that carves-in (i.e., provides 340B drugs to patients with Medicaid fee-for-service).

info

Include out-of-state Medicaid billing numbers and the associated state, if applicable.

Documentation should include the following:

  • List the state(s) billed and corresponding billing number(s) listed on the claims to bill Medicaid fee-for-service for the particular state. Billing number(s) are listed on paper or electronic claims to Medicaid fee-for-service, and may include the billing provider's national provider identifier (NPI) only, the state assigned Medicaid number only, or both the NPI and state assigned Medicaid number.
  • For each covered entity site (340b ID), provide a copy of one Medicaid fee-for-service claim for each state billed. Be prepared to present additional copies of claims during the audit.
  • Describe each state's requirement for billing modifiers
info

Ensure that no protected health information (PHI) or personally identifiable information (PII) such as a patient's name, date of birth, or address is submitted in the data request list uploads.
